Storytime: 12:30–1 p.m. Stay & Play 1–1:30 p.m. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Free. No registration required.

cases.refreshed: The mission is top secret, but we'll tell you this: it's all about balloon cars! Participants will build and experiment with balloon-powered cars, investigate the physics behind how they work, and apply that knowledge to improve their designs! Through demos, interactive learning, and hands-on challenges, students will practice asking questions, making predictions, testing ideas, and discovering how scientific concepts connect to the world around them. All materials are provided, and participants receive their very own kit to take home and continue exploring. Ages 8–11 recommended Materials provided! We believe that STEM is about understanding why things work and applying that understanding for deeper exploration. Our workshops encourage students to think creatively, experiment freely, and learn through hands-on exploration. Learn more about us here: https://stem-sense.wixsite.com/stem-sense

cases.refreshed: Join us in celebrating one of the most important American, female and Black authors in history with a screening of the PBS documentary Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming Space. While best know for her classic novel Their Eyes Were Watching God, this documentary delves deep into Hurston's work as an anthropologist and it's influence on her writing. From the producer: " Raised in the small all-Black Florida town of Eatonville, Zora Neale Hurston studied at Howard University before arriving in New York in 1925. She would soon become a key figure of the Harlem Renaissance, best remembered for her novel, Their Eyes Were Watching God. But even as she gained renown in the Harlem literary circles, Hurston was also discovering anthropology at Barnard College with the renowned Franz Boas. She would make several trips to the American South and the Caribbean, documenting the lives of rural Black people and collecting their stories. She studied her own people, an unusual practice at the time, and during her lifetime became known as the foremost authority on Black folklore. Directed by Tracy Heather Strain, produced by Randall Mac Lowry and executive produced by Cameo George, Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming a Space is an in-depth biography of the influential author whose groundbreaking anthropological work would challenge assumptions about race, gender and cultural superiority that had long defined the field in the 19th century." https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/ameri... Interested in delving deeper into Hurston's work? Join us for February's Short Story Social the Thursday following the screening to discuss her short story "Sweat."
